<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914707_theRebbe_174" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914707_theRebbe_174__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Introductory heading for the maamar on Simchas Torah 5742.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">The day of Simchas Torah 5742.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains that the joy of Simchas Torah is specifically through dancing with the feet, not through intellectual study, and this relates to the letters of the Torah, its lowest level.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">To understand the concept of Simchas Torah,</t>
    <t s="1">and the precise points regarding this are known</t>
    <t s="2">(in the maamar beginning with the words "This" of the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Admor1)</t>
    <t s="3">— that the manner of the joy</t>
    <t s="4">(of Simchas Torah)</t>
    <t s="5">is that we take a Sefer Torah as it is, rolled up and covered with a mantle, and we circle the reading table with it,</t>
    <t s="6">and after circling the reading table, we dance with the Torah.</t>
    <t s="7">For despite the fact that it is written about the Torah2</t>
    <t s="8">that "it is your wisdom and understanding," etc.,</t>
    <t s="9">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="10">the manner of the joy of Simchas Torah is not through study and contemplation,</t>
    <t s="11">understanding and comprehension that are in the head,</t>
    <t s="12">but specifically through dancing with the feet.</t>
    <t s="13">And this concept</t>
    <t s="14">(that Simchas Torah is specifically related to the feet)</t>
    <t s="15">is not only regarding the person</t>
    <t s="16">(that the joy is specifically through dancing with the feet)</t>
    <t s="17">but also regarding the Torah.</t>
    <t s="18">For the joy</t>
    <t s="19">(of Simchas Torah)</t>
    <t s="20">is that Israel rejoices with the letters of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="21">as understood from the fact that the manner of the joy is that we circle the reading table with the Sefer Torah, where throughout the year we read the letters of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="22">and it is known3</t>
    <t s="23">regarding the concept of the four levels TaNaT"A in the Torah, that the letters of the Torah are the lowest level within it,</t>
    <t s="24">the aspect of the "feet" of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="25">And this concept</t>
    <t s="26">(that the joy is in the letters of the Torah)</t>
    <t s="27">is also understood from what is known4</t>
    <t s="28">— that this day is called Simchas Torah because on it we finish the Torah, and it is fitting to rejoice at its completion,</t>
    <t s="29">for this finishing and completing of the Torah</t>
    <t s="30">(on this day)</t>
    <t s="31">is that we then finish and complete the reading of the letters of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="32">For regarding the understanding and comprehension of the Torah, there is no concept of completion or finishing at all,</t>
    <t s="33">since it is "longer than the earth and broader than the sea"5,</t>
    <t s="34">and it is written6</t>
    <t s="35">"and maidens without number" — these are the halachos7.</t>
    <t s="36">For although the halachos that have already been revealed are a specific number,</t>
    <t s="37">"sixty are the queens"6</t>
    <t s="38">— these are the sixty tractates, "and eighty concubines"6</t>
    <t s="39">— these are the eighty baraitos8,</t>
    <t s="40">nevertheless, there is absolutely no end or limit to the halachos that are innovated9.</t>
    <t s="41">For they too were given at Sinai,</t>
    <t s="42">as the statement10</t>
    <t s="43">"Everything that a diligent student will innovate was given to Moshe at Sinai."</t>
    <t s="44">From this it is simply understood that this finishing and completing of the Torah on Simchas Torah is that we finish only the letters of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="45">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="46">regarding the matter of the Torah reading, understanding and comprehension are not relevant,</t>
    <t s="47">for even an ignoramus who does not know what is being said ascends to the Torah and recites the blessing over the Torah11.</t>
    <t s="48">From all this it is understood</t>
    <t s="49">that the joy that we make</t>
    <t s="50">(on Simchas Torah)</t>
    <t s="51">for the completion of the Torah is the joy in the letters of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="52">the aspect of the "feet" of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="53">Therefore, also in the person,</t>
    <t s="54">the joy is specifically through dancing with the feet.</t>
    <t s="55">One must also understand</t>
    <t s="56">(as is precisely noted there in the preceding maamar12)</t>
    <t s="57">why they established Simchas Torah on Shemini Atzeres,</t>
    <t s="58">for ostensibly it should have been made on Shavuos, the time of the giving of our Torah,</t>
    <t s="59">and why do we make Simchas Torah on Shemini Atzeres.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains the connection between Simchas Torah and Shemini Atzeres through a Midrash about the king and his daughters, showing that Shemini Atzeres is a unique holiday for closeness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, this precise point</t>
    <t s="2">(that we make Simchas Torah on Shemini Atzeres and not on Shavuos)</t>
    <t s="3">is addressed in the aforementioned maamar, following the precise point noted there earlier, that regarding Shemini Atzeres it is written13</t>
    <t s="4">"On the eighth day, it shall be an atzeres for you,"</t>
    <t s="5">and yet all the festivals and holy days</t>
    <t s="6">[and likewise all the Torah and mitzvos]</t>
    <t s="7">were given to Israel,</t>
    <t s="8">so why specifically regarding the holiday of Shemini Atzeres does it say "for you,"</t>
    <t s="9">what is the novelty of Shemini Atzeres over all the festivals and holy days?</t>
    <t s="10">And he brings on this,</t>
    <t s="11">that it is stated in the Midrash14,</t>
    <t s="12">"The Atzeres of the Festival [of Sukkos] should have been fifty days distant, corresponding to the Atzeres of Pesach."</t>
    <t s="13">And one could say,</t>
    <t s="14">that by bringing this Midrash that the Atzeres of the Festival should have been fifty days distant like the Atzeres of Pesach,</t>
    <t s="15">the precise point is strengthened</t>
    <t s="16">(that he brings afterwards)</t>
    <t s="17">— why we make Simchas Torah on Shemini Atzeres, when ostensibly it should have been made on Shavuos,</t>
    <t s="18">for from this Midrash it is understood that Shemini Atzeres itself is analogous to Shavuos</t>
    <t s="19">(the Atzeres of Pesach),</t>
    <t s="20">and based on this, it is even less understood why they established Simchas Torah specifically on Shemini Atzeres and not on Shavuos.</t>
    <t s="21">And the Midrash15 explains</t>
    <t s="22">the reason for this, that the Atzeres of the Festival is not fifty days distant,</t>
    <t s="23">"because they are going out from summer to winter, and it is not in their power to go and come [easily]."</t>
    <t s="24">To what can this be compared? To a king who had many daughters,</t>
    <t s="25">some married in a nearby place and some married in a distant place.</t>
    <t s="26">One day, they all came to inquire about the welfare of the king, their father.</t>
    <t s="27">The king said: 'These who are married in a nearby place have the ability to go and come,</t>
    <t s="28">but those who are married in a distant place do not have the ability to go and come.</t>
    <t s="29">Until they are all here with me, let us make one festival and rejoice with them.'</t>
    <t s="30">So too, regarding the Atzeres of Pesach,</t>
    <t s="31">since they are going out from winter to summer, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'They have the ability to go and come.'</t>
    <t s="32">But regarding the Atzeres of the Festival, because they are going out from summer to winter, etc., the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'They do not have the ability to go and come,</t>
    <t s="33">but until they are here, let us make one festival and rejoice.'</t>
    <t s="34">Therefore, Moshe warns Israel: 'On the eighth day, it shall be an atzeres for you.'"</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
